correctness.rationale: On all six faces the proposed distance function is the minimum of feasible unfolded Euclidean distances, agrees on glued edges, and is 1-Lipschitz in every face. Hence it globally lower-bounds intrinsic length while feasible two-square unfoldings attain it. The opposite-face formula and the reduction to a unit square and a precise right triangle follow. Angular bounds integrate to the three arcsine density branches and the CDF constants; the 3/2 moment follows by conditioning on near/opposite faces. One-sided derivatives give jumps -1,-1,+5/6; a triangular corner wedge gives the 5/12 sharp terminal tail. An actually executed standard-library verification program checked the CDF against separate Cartesian-area integrals, 300000 sampled surface points, and independent moments and tails. The proof, not finite sampling, certifies all radii.

value.rationale: The complete intrinsic vertex-to-uniform-surface distance distribution is a canonical metric-measure invariant of a basic convex polyhedral surface. Its two nontrivial internal radii are exactly distance shells containing other cube vertices (1 and sqrt(2)), with explicit discontinuities of F double prime, plus a distinct sharp quadratic cutoff at sqrt(5). The angular cancellations reduce a six-face wavefront calculation to two closed arcsine branches. This is more informative than one isolated moment or routine distance conversion and supplies an exact calibration benchmark for discrete geodesics. The claim is the complete natural law, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
